title: A timed-out mutation loses its already-captured rollback state
test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'a mutation whose response times out after dispatch is still rolled back' (VAL-112; also 'a mutation that throws after dispatch is journaled once'; guards that passed before and after: 'a mutation OBS explicitly rejects is not journaled', 'a mutation that was never dispatched because its snapshot failed is not journaled')
proof: Holds. createObsConfigurationTransaction.request captured the inverse with snapshotMutation, then awaited sendRequest and pushed the inverse onto rollbackSteps only after a successful answer; sendRequest rejects when the 5 s request deadline passes (obsWebSocket.js:86-89), and that rejection left request() before the push, so a SetVideoSettings (or any snapshotted mutation) that OBS applied late was never restored and rollback() returned [] as if nothing were open. The first test runs a real withObsConnection against a fake OBS socket (requestTimeoutMs 20) whose first SetVideoSettings is applied but never answered in time, then calls rollback(); on the unchanged code it failed at the final assertion: the requests OBS received held only the 1280x720 write, the expected restore to the snapshot (1920x1080) was missing. The second test (a sendRequest that throws on the first SetStreamServiceSettings) failed with '1 !== 2' writes. Fix: request() wraps the dispatch in try/catch; on a throw it pushes the captured inverse onto rollbackSteps and rethrows the same error. The success path is unchanged and there is one push per request (no double entry); a response with requestStatus.result false is still returned without journaling; a request whose snapshot call throws or fails never reaches the dispatch and is not journaled; rollback still uses the raw sendRequest. A timed-out StartStream or StopStream has no captured state (its inverse is the opposite request) and is left as before.

title: Rollback of profile parameters that were unset writes an empty string instead of restoring the default
test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'rolling back an unset profile parameter sends null so OBS deletes it' (VAL-113)
proof: Holds. snapshotMutation built the SetProfileParameter inverse with parameterValue: String(previous.responseData?.parameterValue ?? ''), so a parameter OBS reports as unset (GetProfileParameter answers parameterValue null and the default in defaultParameterValue) was restored as an explicit empty string; obs-websocket v5 deletes the parameter when SetProfileParameter gets null. The new test runs the transaction over a fake OBS socket: AdvOut/Encoder answers null, Video/ColorRange answers 'Full'; both are changed and rolled back, and the SetProfileParameter payloads OBS receives are compared. On the unchanged code it failed with the Encoder restore carrying parameterValue '' where null was expected (the ColorRange restore, 'Full', was right). Fix: the snapshot uses normalizeProfileValue (null stays null, anything else becomes a string), and the payload goes out with parameterValue null (JSON null survives the wire). A set value still round-trips as a string (the existing rollback tests pass unchanged).
